newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norwegian shares flat in lacklustre activity.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian shares flat in lacklustre activity.

text.p: Norwegian shares traded in a narrow band on Wednesday and ended mainly flat in thin business ahead of the Ascension Day break on Thursday.

Investors had been cautious all week due to the pubic holiday and before April's domestic inflation figure due on Friday. The government also is due to present this year's revised budget next Tuesday.
Oslo's Total share index closed a marginal 0.11 percent up at the day's high at 1,106.50 points. The index traded in a slim band down to 1,102.88 points. Volume was just 779 million crowns.
"It was a day with no major events and a lot of numbers that didn't move the market," said one dealer.
Cruise company NCL Holdings was the most traded share accounting for 75.2 million crowns of trade and gained 0.70 crowns to 18.80 crowns.

"It seems like investors are looking for stocks that haven't moved recently," said one broker on the NCL activity. "It also appears that faith is returning to some of the technology shares that have been out of favour lately," he added.
Blue-chip of the technologies, Tomra, climbed a hefty 14 crowns to 154 in turnover of 42.3 million crowns.
